summary: The prepared implementation already runs two eager model forwards before entering the CUDA graph context, so first-dispatch DeepEP buffer creation occurs outside capture. This ordering also predates the issue's latest update. No issue-specific runtime defect was demonstrated, and the shared deep_ep.cpp:230 signature can also result from an unchecked NVSHMEM allocation OOM.

tests.what_was_measured: The actual FullCudaGraphBackend.capture_one invoked the focused forward with capture states [false, false, true], performed one lazy GPU allocation, and replayed with max_abs_error=0.0 against an independent CPU reference.
The prepared ROCm interpreter lacks the DeepEP extension (ModuleNotFoundError), explicitly bounding the investigation.

gpu_execution_evidence: Actual SGLang FullCudaGraphBackend capture and replay ran on AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950), with capture_state=[false,false,true], one eager lazy allocation, and exact numerical output.
remaining_limitations: No H800/CUDA host, DeepEP extension, NVSHMEM/InfiniBand topology, Kimi K2.6 W4A8 weights, or 2-node x 8-GPU PP=2/TP=8/DP=8/EP=8 environment was available. The GPU fixture validates graph ordering only, not DeepEP communication, Kimi semantics, quantization, pipeline parallelism, or the reported distributed workload.
